_session_user_comment: The account the fixture session is signed in as; the status strip resolves it to a display name for its user cell.
_login_comment: Accounts offered by the login dialog's user combo. The capture seeds these
into a hermetic settings store instead of reading the real per-user list,
so client-login.png never leaks the capturing machine's accounts. The first
entry is also the pre-selected user.
_filesystem_comment: The file store the Files view (FileSystemView) lists: instance nodes under the FileSystem folder (SCADA.304), directories typed FileDirectoryType (SCADA.305) and files typed FileType (SCADA.306). Ids follow what the server's MakeNodeId produces — a string id in the FILESYSTEM_FILE namespace holding the URL-escaped path, hence the %2F in a nested entry. Without these the view renders its root row and nothing else, which is how files.png shipped.
_display_comment: VDS/SDE fixture for the reshelled substation display (CaptureDisplay), relative to this file.

display._measurements_comment: Signals pushed into the display frame's Measurements strip, standing in for the elements an operator clicks on the diagram.

nodes._comment: The device's diagnostic variables are wired a second time as HasComponent (NS0.47), on top of the Organizes edge the `tree` block gives every fixture child. A real device instance carries its data variables as components, and GetDataVariables (common/node_service/node_util.cpp) reads HasComponent and nothing else - so the service-object dialog, which lists a device's components, renders an empty list against an Organizes-only fixture. The Organizes edge stays: it is what puts these variables in the object tree.

Second controllable analog, sibling of TIT.212, whose output condition is NOT met: TIT.211 sits at 42.3, so `TIT.211 > 70` evaluates false and the control dialog renders its condition row as unsatisfied with OK disabled. It is a separate node because one node cannot render the satisfied and unsatisfied variants in a single run; the ti-remote-control-disabled.png dialog spec names it through `node`.

The fixture's only discrete data items, and the reason the ts-*-control captures render the TS dialog instead of a second copy of the TI one: WriteModel takes its discrete branch from TimedDataSpec::logical(), which tests DiscreteItemType, and its two state labels from the HasTsFormat (SCADA.154) target. They live in the TS namespace, which is DiscreteItemType's own (namespaces.csv), under the ЭСТРА-ПС «ТС» folder. base_value 0 reads back as the format's OpenLabel («Вкл»), and the combo pre-selects the opposite state («Откл») — the current-then-command direction the docs originals show. TS.201 is the satisfied-condition node, `TIT.211 < 70` being true over the fixture data; TS.202 is its unsatisfied sibling, the same split TIT.212/TIT.213 make on the analog side.

_local_events_comment: Client-side events, reported through LocalEvents. The journal renders these with the object «Локальное событие» rather than a node display name, which is what the manual's event-journal pages show. severity is info | warning | error.
_events_comment: severity is either a band literal (normal/warning/critical) or a raw OPC UA severity in 1..1000; the numeric form exists because three literals cannot name a value that sits deliberately between the bands. These are server history events — the client-side ones the manual shows under the object «Локальное событие» are seeded from the separate local_events array below.

_screenshots_comment: Filenames track the docs image names where possible so the output is
a drop-in replacement for the current docs images. Dimensions
follow the docs images; if there is no matching docs image yet the
size is a reasonable default. The image manifest reference
column maps each filename to the markdown page(s) that embed it.
Every row carries exactly one of `type` and `capture`, and Load asserts
it. `type` is a registered WindowInfo name: the row becomes a window on
the generator's profile page. `capture` is a standalone capture key,
dispatched in CaptureAllWindows the way `kind` is in the dialogs array,
and such a row never reaches the page. Keep capture keys kebab-case so
the two can never be confused for each other.
The sixth path of both Table captures ("TIT.999") is deliberately a node
id that appears in neither `nodes` nor `tree`, so the row renders the
"Нет данных" (no data) state the manual documents. Keep it nonexistent —
if TIT.999 is ever added to the fixture, move these captures to another
unused id rather than dropping the row.
_dialogs_comment: Modal-dialog captures. Each entry's `kind` is dispatched in the
CaptureDialogs TEST_F to build the right dialog class with its own
fixture. Filenames and dimensions track image_manifest.json.
width/height are optional and only resize dialogs that can be resized;
omit them for self-sizing dialogs such as message boxes, whose layout

dialogs._comment: The «Создание сервисных объектов» modal, which the object tree opens on a folder and which the manual embeds as menu-create-object.png's sibling. Distinct from multi-create above: that one builds a series of new TS/TI from a naming pattern, this one mirrors an existing device's diagnostic variables into service data items, so its list is the device's components rather than a generated range. The size is the form's own designed geometry (create_service_item.ui).

_device_log_comment: Device-log lines for the Log (device watch) capture, delivered as event notifications on `device`. An entry with a `frame` object arrives as a DeviceFrameEventType event and fills the decoded columns; one without is a plain log line, which is also what an older server sends - the #/$ marker then drives the direction column through the client's fallback.

_favourites_comment: Saved windows for the Favorites pane. `type` is the registered window-type name (Table, Graph, ...) — it is what FavouritesWindowNode::GetIcon maps to a glyph, so a fixture with both kinds is what proves the table and graph icons differ. Entries with no folder sit at the root.
